memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Judah saw her, he thought she was a prostitute, for she had covered her face. Not realizing that she was his daughter-in-law, he went over to her by the roadside and said, 'Come now, let me sleep with you.' 'And what will you give me to sleep with you?' she asked. 'I'll send you a young goat from my flock,' he said. 'Will you give me something as a pledge until you send it?' she asked. He said, 'What pledge should I give you?' 'Your seal and its cord, and the staff in your hand,' she answered. So he gave them to her and slept with her, and she became pregnant by him." - Gen 38:15-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here we see Judah's own sin laid bare. Taking the veiled woman for a prostitute, he propositions her without hesitation, agreeing to pay with a young goat and leaving his personal seal and staff as a pledge. These items were like an identity card — unmistakably his. Judah, the man who had wronged Tamar, now falls into sexual sin himself, never dreaming who the woman truly is.

There is a heavy irony building here. Judah, who had treated Tamar as expendable, is now caught in a moment of loose living that will expose his own hypocrisy. The very pledge he hands over will one day become the evidence that condemns his double standard.

The passage quietly warns us about a dangerous blindness: it is easy to condemn sin in others while excusing it in ourselves. Judah would soon be ready to punish Tamar harshly, all while guilty of sin himself. We are often harshest toward the faults of others and blindest to our own.

Jesus put His finger on this: "Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother's eye and pay no attention to the plank in your own eye?" (Matt 7:3). Before we rush to judge another, let us look honestly at ourselves. The God who sees Tamar's sin sees Judah's too — and He sees ours. Humility before God begins with honesty about our own hearts.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I harder on others' sins than on my own?
2. Where might I be blind to a "plank" in my own eye?
3. How can I grow in honest humility before God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from the blindness of condemning others while excusing myself. Help me to see the plank in my own eye, and to walk humbly, honest about my own need for Your grace. Amen.
